# FIPS 140-3 crypto module remediation for KServe serving images

## Description

This epic makes the KServe serving stack's images run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in the request
path. It delivers the remediated KServe serving images (serverless and raw deployment data
plane surfaces), together with the per-image crypto module inventory, build attestations,
and FIPS-enabled-cluster test results that the compliance evidence package consolidates.

## Scope

- Audit the KServe serving images to inventory the cryptographic libraries each image
  links, recording which are validated and which are non-validated (the strategy identifies
  that several images currently link non-validated crypto libraries).
- Replace non-validated crypto library usage in the KServe serving images with validated
  cryptographic modules, covering both serverless and raw deployment data plane surfaces
  (predictor, and the request path generally).
- Rebuild the remediated images through the standard build pipeline, retaining build
  attestations.
- Verify the remediated images on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters: InferenceServices
  deploy, serve inference requests correctly, and the request path uses only validated
  crypto modules.
- Produce the KServe portion of the crypto module inventory and the FIPS test results as
  evidence inputs for the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, when an InferenceService is deployed in serverless
  mode and in raw deployment mode, then the serving data plane handles requests using
  validated cryptographic modules and no non-validated crypto is used in the request path
  (measured by: crypto module audit of each serving image, and functional inference tests
  on a FIPS-enabled cluster).
- Given the crypto module audit, when the inventory is produced, then every cryptographic
  library linked into each KServe serving image is listed with its validated/non-validated
  status, and every non-validated usage found is either replaced or explicitly justified as
  outside the request path.
- Given the remediated images, when they are built through the standard build pipeline,
  then the builds are green and build attestations are retained for the evidence package.
- Given the remediated images deployed on a FIPS-enabled cluster, when inference requests
  are served, then responses are correct and serving behavior is unchanged relative to the
  pre-remediation baseline.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using
  validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path) — this epic covers
  the KServe serving images and data plane surfaces.

## Risks and Assumptions

- Assumes remediation can land in the midstream KServe repositories the team controls; if
  changes are required upstream in kserve/kserve, upstream coordination would extend this
  epic's timeline (not indicated by the strategy).
- The set of affected images is discovered by the audit; the epic's structure and approach
  do not change based on the audit outcome (audit → remediate → verify).

# FIPS 140-3 crypto module remediation for the Platform Operator

## Description

This epic makes the Platform Operator and its deployment of the model serving stack run
correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. It
delivers the remediated operator image, verification that the operator deploys the serving
stack successfully on FIPS-enabled clusters, and the operator's crypto module inventory,
build attestations, and test results as evidence inputs for the compliance evidence
package.

## Scope

- Audit the Platform Operator image to inventory the cryptographic libraries it links,
  recording which are validated and which are non-validated.
- Replace non-validated crypto library usage in the operator image with validated
  cryptographic modules so that the operator itself runs correctly on FIPS-enabled
  clusters.
- Verify on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters that the operator installs and reconciles the
  model serving stack (KServe and related serving components) without errors and that the
  deployed serving stack functions per the FIPS support posture.
- Rebuild the remediated operator image through the standard build pipeline, retaining
  build attestations.
- Produce the Platform Operator portion of the crypto module inventory and the FIPS test
  results as evidence inputs for the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, when the Platform Operator is installed and
  reconciles the model serving stack, then the operator runs using validated cryptographic
  modules and completes deployment without errors (measured by: crypto module audit of the
  operator image, and operator functional tests on a FIPS-enabled cluster).
- Given the remediated operator image, when it is built through the standard build
  pipeline, then the build is green and build attestations are retained for the evidence
  package.
- Given a FIPS-enabled cluster, when serving components are deployed through the operator,
  then the deployed serving stack behaves correctly relative to the pre-remediation
  baseline.
- Given the crypto module audit, when the inventory is produced, then every cryptographic
  library linked into the operator image is listed with its validated/non-validated status,
  and every non-validated usage is replaced.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using
  validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path) — this epic covers
  the Platform Operator image and the operator's deployment of the serving stack.

## Risks and Assumptions

- The strategy lists Platform Operator as an affected component but does not describe its
  specific change; this epic assumes the change is FIPS crypto remediation of the operator
  image plus deployment verification, consistent with HLR-1's "all serving-stack images".
  No architecture context file was provisioned for this component, so its scope should be
  verified by the owning team.
- Assumes the operator repository is under the team's control and no upstream coordination
  is required (not indicated otherwise by the strategy).

# CI gating check enforcing FIPS crypto compliance in serving-stack builds

## Description

This epic adds a gating check to the serving-stack build pipelines so that any build which
reintroduces non-validated crypto usage into a serving-stack image fails the build. It
delivers the check itself, wired into the build pipeline configuration for serving-stack
builds, providing continuous enforcement against FIPS regressions after the remediated
images are in place.

## Scope

- Implement a check that detects non-validated crypto usage in serving-stack build outputs
  (images), consistent with the validated/non-validated module boundary established by the
  crypto module audits of the serving stack.
- Wire the check into the build pipeline configuration so it runs on serving-stack builds
  (KServe serving images and the Platform Operator image).
- Enable the check as a gating check: a build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage
  fails. Activation is coordinated with the availability of remediated images, since the
  gate is defined against builds that "reintroduce" non-validated crypto — i.e., the
  compliant baseline must exist before the gate is enforced.
- Document the check's failure output so a failed build identifies the offending
  non-validated crypto usage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the gating check is enabled on serving-stack builds, when a build reintroduces
  non-validated crypto usage into a serving-stack image, then the build fails and the
  failure identifies the offending crypto usage (measured by: a build of an image
  deliberately containing non-validated crypto fails; a build of a compliant image passes).
- Given a compliant serving-stack image build, when the check runs, then the build passes.
- Given the remediated serving-stack images are available as the compliant baseline, when
  the check is activated, then it is enabled as a gating (not advisory-only) check on
  serving-stack builds.
- Given any serving-stack build (KServe or Platform Operator image), when it runs, then the
  check executes as part of the build.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: CI enforces FIPS regressions — a gating check fails any serving-stack
  build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

## Risks and Assumptions

- Assumes the check's detection criteria can be expressed from the validated/non-validated
  module classification used in the serving-stack audits; the implementing team selects the
  concrete detection mechanism.
- The check must not be enabled as a gate before compliant images exist, or it would fail
  every serving-stack build; activation ordering is an acceptance criterion, not a reason
  to serialize this work behind the remediation.
- Wiring the check into the Platform Operator's build pipeline spans a component owned by
  a different team (the Platform Operator is owned by RHOAI Platform); landing that wiring
  likely requires coordination with that team — verify ownership of the operator build
  pipeline configuration before assignment.

# Compliance evidence package assembly and submission to the security review board and certification lab

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving stack
— consolidating the serving stack's crypto module inventories, build attestations, and
FIPS-enabled-cluster test results — and submits it through the security review board to the
external accredited certification laboratory. The epic's completion is bounded by human and
third-party process gates: mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones,
and laboratory scheduling with a historical turnaround of six to nine months. The
certification decision itself is externally controlled and is not a deliverable of this
epic.

## Scope

- Consolidate the crypto module inventories, build attestations, and test results produced
  by the serving-stack FIPS remediation work (KServe serving images and the Platform
  Operator image) into a single compliance evidence package.
- Structure the package to satisfy the security review board's evidence requirements for
  the defined sign-off milestones (the strategy gives no board-requirements artifact; the
  epic includes eliciting/confirming those requirements as part of its work).
- Obtain the mandatory security review board sign-off at each defined milestone.
- Submit the package to the external accredited certification laboratory and confirm the
  submission is accepted.
- Track the submission through the external process; report lab scheduling and review-board
  cadence as externally controlled constraints that engineering cannot compress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the remediation evidence inputs are available, when the package is assembled, then
  it contains the module inventory, build attestations, and test results for every
  serving-stack image in scope (measured by: package contents reviewed against the scope of
  serving-stack images).
- Given the assembled package, when it is presented at each defined milestone, then the
  security review board sign-off is recorded for that milestone.
- Given a board-approved package, when it is submitted to the external certification lab,
  then the submission is accepted and acknowledged by the laboratory.
- Given any gap identified by the board or lab in the evidence, when the gap is reported,
  then the missing evidence is produced and resubmitted (fix-and-retry; the epic does not
  promise the certification decision or its timing).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations,
  test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the
  external certification lab.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Human and third-party gates dominate the schedule**: the security review board signs
  off at defined milestones and the external accredited laboratory has a six-to-nine-month
  historical turnaround; both are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by
  engineering effort. This epic sequences and shepherds those gates; it does not control
  them.
- The certification decision and its timing rest with the external laboratory and are
  intentionally outside this epic's acceptance criteria.
- The strategy provides no board evidence-requirements specification; requirements
  elicitation is included in scope and may reshape package formatting (not the underlying
  evidence, which is fixed by the remediation outputs).
- The package consolidates evidence produced by the Platform Operator remediation, a
  component owned by a different team (RHOAI Platform); collecting and validating the
  operator's inventory, attestations, and test results likely requires coordination with
  that team — verify evidence ownership with both teams before assignment.

# Document the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites

## Description

This epic authors the customer-facing documentation for the model serving stack's FIPS
140-3 support: what the FIPS support posture is (which serving-stack images run with
validated crypto modules on FIPS-enabled clusters, and the status of the external
certification effort) and what cluster prerequisites apply (FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster
requirements). The documentation is written after the implementation work it describes, and
is technically reviewed against that implementation.

## Scope

- Author new documentation topics stating the model serving stack's FIPS support posture,
  including the scope of serving-stack images covered and the relationship to the external
  certification process (in progress vs. certified), phrased so it remains accurate as the
  certification status evolves.
- Author documentation of cluster prerequisites for running the serving stack with
